uncited: *   **Input:** A volume dataset (density and opacity fields), a camera projection matrix, and a screen-space opacity buffer initialized to zero.
*   **Opacity Buffer:** A 2D array matching the screen resolution, storing the accumulated opacity $\alpha_{acc}$ for each pixel.
*   **Bounding Box:** A 2D integer rectangle $(x_{min}, y_{min}, x_{max}, y_{max})$ defining the pixel coverage of a projected voxel.
**Check Opacity:** Iterate through all pixels within the bounding box.
Let $B$ be the set of pixel coordinates in the bounding box.
Let $\alpha_{acc}(p)$ be the accumulated opacity at pixel $p$.
The exact value depends on floating-point precision and desired visual fidelity.
A ray-casting optimization that stops ray traversal when accumulated opacity reaches a threshold.
A sibling optimization that skips splats based on their projected footprint size.
It differs from Early Splat Termination by using geometric bounds rather than accumulated opacity [2849-splat-size-culling.md].
*   **Time Complexity:** The check is $O(A)$ where $A$ is the area of the bounding box in pixels.
In the worst case (no termination), it adds overhead to every voxel.
In the best case (full opacity), it saves the cost of splatting.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Requires an additional screen-space opacity buffer, $O(W \times H)$ where $W, H$ are screen dimensions.
